base_paper_title: Multi-Modal Point-of-Care Diagnostics for COVID-19 Based on Acoustics and Symptoms
venue: IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: Coswara cough, breathing, speech, and symptoms with subject-disjoint internal evaluation.
paper_results_concise: Published final article: three-audio fusion AUC 0.88. Audio plus symptoms AUC 0.963 in the abstract and 0.96 after rounding in the results.
our_exact_comparison: Our multimodal audio AUROC was 0.8489 +/- 0.0195 with fold-wise feature selection, 0.8641 +/- 0.0195 with the fixed top-800 feature bank, and 0.8949 for the primary equal-weight participant split. The exploratory stack reached 0.8971. The +/- values are fold standard deviations.
our_contribution_or_defense: The fixed-feature result is 0.0159 below their audio-only result and the primary source-split result is 0.0149 higher. Our study additionally evaluates temporal stability, frozen external transfer, calibration, and metadata dependence.
important_comparison_boundary: Their 0.963 result includes symptoms and must not be compared with an audio-only result. Dataset snapshot, preprocessing, models, and split implementation also differ.

base_paper_title: Fused Audio Instance and Representation for Respiratory Disease Detection
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: Coswara multimodal evaluation using seven respiratory recordings represented as waveforms and spectrograms. A fixed 226-participant test set was used with five rotating development folds repeated using two seeds.
paper_results_concise: Cough plus breath plus speech AUC 0.8658 +/- 0.0115, reported as mean +/- standard deviation across the repeated development experiments.
our_exact_comparison: Our clean fold-local multimodal AUROC was 0.8489 +/- 0.0195. Our fixed-feature sensitivity AUROC was 0.8641 +/- 0.0195. The +/- values are fold standard deviations.
our_contribution_or_defense: The fixed-feature result is only 0.0017 lower. The cleaner fold-local estimate is 0.0169 lower. Our study extends internal evaluation with temporal, confounding, calibration, and external-transfer analyses.
important_comparison_boundary: The fixed-feature result is a sensitivity analysis because feature selection was not repeated inside every fold. Cohort snapshot, representations, and testing design differ.

base_paper_title: COVID-19 Detection From Respiratory Sounds With Hierarchical Spectrogram Transformers
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: HST was trained and evaluated within a balanced COUGHVID cough task containing 1644 COVID and 1644 non-COVID samples. Ten-fold cross-validation used nearly 70% training, 20% testing, and 10% validation with no participant overlap.
paper_results_concise: COUGHVID internal test AUC 0.90 +/- 0.01, precision 0.80 +/- 0.03, recall 0.84 +/- 0.03, and F1 0.82 +/- 0.01. Values are mean +/- standard deviation across cross-validation folds.
our_exact_comparison: Our primary Coswara equal-weight multimodal AUROC was 0.8949 on 314 test participants; the exploratory stack reached 0.8971. Frozen Coswara-to-COUGHVID cough AUROC was 0.5226 to 0.5428 on 8331 recording UUIDs. WavLM external AUROC was 0.4837 and CNN-BiGRU external AUROC was 0.5484.
comparison_type: Architecture context rather than direct transfer comparison
our_contribution_or_defense: HST shows that COUGHVID is internally learnable when target data are available for training. Our contribution is testing whether Coswara-trained conventional, transformer-based, and spectrogram representations transport without COUGHVID training.
important_comparison_boundary: HST internal COUGHVID performance and our frozen Coswara-to-COUGHVID transfer answer different questions and must not be subtracted as a fair performance gap.

base_paper_title: Robust COVID-19 Detection From Cough Sounds Using Deep Neural Decision Tree and Forest: A Comprehensive Cross-Datasets Evaluation
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: The paper evaluated selected Coswara and COUGHVID cough cohorts internally and performed explicit train-on-one and test-on-another transfer using its best DNDF strategy.
paper_results_concise: Best DNDF internal AUC 0.92 on Coswara and 0.93 on COUGHVID. Coswara-to-COUGHVID transfer AUC 0.53.
our_exact_comparison: Our matched Coswara cough source AUROC was 0.8494 to 0.8679. Our frozen COUGHVID AUROC was 0.5226 to 0.5428 across CatBoost, LightGBM, SVC, and XGBoost.
our_contribution_or_defense: Their 0.53 is essentially identical to our external range. Our study adds independent-bootstrap uncertainty, calibration, high-sensitivity operating points, learned-representation checks, and evaluation on all 8331 retained COUGHVID recording UUIDs.
important_comparison_boundary: Their selected target and our naturally imbalanced pseudo-labeled target differ. Participant grouping and target composition are not identical.

base_paper_title: Sounds of COVID-19: Exploring Realistic Performance of Audio-Based Digital Testing
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: Participant-independent and demographically controlled evaluation used 5240 samples from 2478 English-speaking participants, with deliberately biased protocol variants examined separately.
paper_results_concise: Controlled multimodal AUC-ROC 0.71 with 95% CI 0.65 to 0.77. Less appropriate biased settings reached AUC 0.90 with 95% CI 0.85 to 0.95.
our_exact_comparison: Our primary internal AUROC was 0.8949. Our early-to-late top-four breath ensemble had mean AUROC 0.6908 +/- 0.0066 across three seeds.
our_contribution_or_defense: Our temporal estimate is close to their controlled estimate. Both studies show that favorable internal results can decrease under stricter cohort construction. We add frozen external transfer, calibration, feature stability, and shuffled-label controls.
important_comparison_boundary: Different datasets and different controls prevent a model-performance ranking. The valid comparison concerns the effect of evaluation design.

base_paper_title: Audio-Based AI Classifiers Show No Evidence of Improved COVID-19 Screening Over Simple Symptoms Checkers
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: A PCR-referenced UK cohort of 67842 individuals was evaluated using unadjusted and measured-confounder-matched protocols. Audio models were also compared with symptom-based prediction.
paper_results_concise: Unadjusted ROC-AUC 0.846 with 95% CI 0.838 to 0.854. Matched ROC-AUC 0.619 with 95% CI 0.594 to 0.644. Symptom-based prediction outperformed the evaluated audio classifier in practical analyses.
our_exact_comparison: Our internal AUROC was 0.8489 to 0.8971, temporal mean AUROC was 0.6908, and frozen external AUROC was 0.5226 to 0.5428. Full context predicted source labels at AUROC 0.9638. Our aligned incremental audio analysis was inconclusive with only 58 to 61 participants.
our_contribution_or_defense: Their work is stronger for PCR labels, cohort size, enrollment design, and symptoms comparison. Our complementary contribution is public source-to-target transfer, repeated model-family evidence, calibration under shift, temporal feature stability, and explicit source-context analysis.
important_comparison_boundary: Our COUGHVID endpoint is a semi-supervised pseudo-label and cannot match their clinical label quality. Our incremental-value sample is too small to claim equivalence or improvement over symptoms.

base_paper_title: A Comprehensive Drift-Adaptive Framework for Sustaining Model Performance in COVID-19 Detection From Dynamic Cough Audio Data: Model Development and Validation
paper_dataset_and_evaluation: Chronological 70:30 development-to-postdevelopment evaluation with drift detection and adaptation on dynamic Coswara and COVID-19 Sounds cough streams.
paper_results_concise: Coswara baseline AUC-ROC decreased from 0.668 in development to 0.597 in postdevelopment data. COVID-19 Sounds decreased from 0.691 to 0.607.
our_exact_comparison: Our early-to-late top-four breath ensemble had mean AUROC 0.6908 +/- 0.0066 across three seeds. Early-versus-late top-800 feature overlap had Jaccard index 0.074.
our_contribution_or_defense: Their work is stronger on online drift detection and adaptation. Our contribution is connecting temporal degradation with feature-ranking instability, metadata predictability, calibration behavior, and independent external transfer.
important_comparison_boundary: Our temporal analysis is retrospective and does not implement online adaptation. Calendar cohorts differ strongly in prevalence, so the result is evidence of instability rather than a causal effect of viral evolution.
